agree.reason: Mark gets a likeable, candid memo, but nothing in it shifts his belief that the renovation drove the scores (the 7.9→8.2 pre-renovation rise is missing), and it never makes a case against the outside candidate, so he probably stays undecided.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the 'main reason' claim and admits the renovation helped, but 'the department has stayed stable' is vague and unsupported, and the savings claims in the budget plan are asserted rather than shown.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out 'almost half' the training time and 'four more people' kept, but it leaves out the strongest true number (the 8.2 reached before the renovation began), never turns turnover into rates (64% down to 36%), and leaves a placeholder where the coverage results should go (no uncovered shifts, overtime under plan).

right_comparison.reason: It never compares Daniela with the outside candidate, and it sets the renovation against her work by assertion instead of showing the score trend before and after the renovation started.

qualification.reason: The budget plan has a 30-day step and monthly reviews, but it doesn't name the finance course with its 3-month deadline or the controller's weekly sessions, and it sets no measurable bar or consequence if the bar is missed.

objections.reason: It names the budget gap honestly, but it meets the renovation objection only with reasoning, not the available evidence, and it ignores the larger-hotel candidate completely.

fit.reason: It is a one-page memo as asked, but the name placeholders (including the GM's and the controller's, which the writer had) and the '[add specifics]' gap mean it isn't ready to send.
